english: The parabolas $y^{2}=8x$ and $x^{2}=-8y$ have exactly one common normal. If this common normal meets the $y$-axis at the point $(0,\beta)$, then the value of $\beta$ is ______.
hindi: परवलयों $y^{2}=8x$ तथा $x^{2}=-8y$ का ठीक एक उभयनिष्ठ अभिलम्ब है। यदि यह उभयनिष्ठ अभिलम्ब $y$-अक्ष को बिन्दु $(0,\beta)$ पर मिलता है, तो $\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Normal to $x^{2}=-8y$ at $(4s,-2s^{2})$: tangent slope $-s$, so $y=\dfrac{x}{s}-4-2s^{2}$.
The quartic factor is positive ($s^{4}+s^{3}+3s^{2}+s+1=\left(s^{2}+\frac s2\right)^{2}+\frac{11}{4}s^{2}+s+1>0$), so $s=1$, $m=1$: $y=x-6$.
(The vertex normal $y=0$ of the first parabola is not normal to the second.) Hence $\beta=-6$.
solution_full: For $y^{2}=4ax$ with $a=2$, the normal with slope $m$ is $y=mx-2am-am^{3}=mx-4m-2m^{3}$; it is normal at $(2m^{2},-4m)$. The case $m=0$ is the axis $y=0$.

For $x^{2}=-8y$, i.e. $y=-\dfrac{x^{2}}{8}$, take the point $(4s,-2s^{2})$. Then $y'=-\dfrac{x}{4}=-s$, so for $s\neq0$ the normal has slope $\dfrac1s$: $y+2s^{2}=\dfrac1s(x-4s)$, i.e. $y=\dfrac{x}{s}-4-2s^{2}$. At $s=0$ the normal is $x=0$.
The line $y=0$ is not of the second form and $x=0$ is not of the first, so a common normal needs $m=\dfrac1s$ and equal intercepts: $-\dfrac4s-\dfrac{2}{s^{3}}=-4-2s^{2}$.

$s^{4}+s^{3}+3s^{2}+s+1=\left(s^{2}+\dfrac{s}{2}\right)^{2}+\dfrac{11}{4}s^{2}+s+1$, and $\dfrac{11}{4}s^{2}+s+1$ has discriminant $1-11<0$, so the quartic has no real root. Hence $s=1$ and $m=1$ only.
The common normal is $y=x-6$ (normal to $y^{2}=8x$ at $(2,-4)$ and to $x^{2}=-8y$ at $(4,-2)$). It is symmetric about the line $y=-x$, which maps one parabola to the other, as expected.
originality_note: New: common normal of two parabolas that are reflections of each other in y = -x, solved through the slope form of one and the parametric form of the other; uniqueness needs a quintic factorisation (way 5). Closest known: common normal of y^2 = 4ax and x^2 = 4by type problems. Different because: the uniqueness argument (quartic factor positive) is part of the question's claim and the line is found by matching two different normal forms.
blueprint_concepts: Normal to the parabola: point, slope and parametric forms

concept_use.Common tangent/normal between two curves: Equating the normal y = mx - 4m - 2m^3 with y = x/s - 4 - 2s^2 for both parabolas gives the single common normal y = x - 6.
concept_use.Normal to the parabola: point, slope and: Slope form of the normal of y^2 = 8x and parametric (4s,-2s^2) normal of x^2 = -8y.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (negative integer); Hindi mirrors the English maths. Uniqueness of the common normal stated in the stem and verified (quartic factor positive). No change.
key_step: Equate the slope-form normal of one parabola with the parametric normal of the other and factor the quintic at s = 1.
justification: Standard normal forms chained with a factorisation; the uniqueness is given in the stem so the student only needs the real root s = 1, making it a routine numerical (L2, like 2023-P1-Q7), below the L4 parabola-normal anchor 2024-P2-Q12 which has a hidden ratio.
